plan.expected_behavior: Out-of-fold target construction should reduce self-induced early-exercise errors and improve realized discounted payoff relative to the parent’s in-sample backward recursion. Ridge regularization and compact symmetry-aware features should remain stable with 256 paths and fit comfortably within 30 seconds. The intervention is mechanistically motivated; the prior gated-ridge score is supporting context, not causal proof.
plan.failure_condition: It can fail when positive-payoff samples are extremely rare, when the true continuation boundary depends on interactions omitted by the compact features, or when fold-level target noise dominates the reduction in in-sample bias. In those cases, the learned rule may exercise too early; detect this through low positive-sample counts or materially worse pooled out-of-fold policy payoff than a never-exercise-until-maturity baseline.
plan.implementation: Run backward induction with 8 deterministic folds. At each time, fit standardized ridge regressions on the other seven folds using only paths whose immediate payoff is positive; select lambda from {0.001,0.01,0.1,1,10} by pooled out-of-fold squared error. Predict each held-out fold and update its cash flow only when immediate payoff exceeds the out-of-fold continuation estimate. After constructing these cross-fitted cash-flow targets, refit one ridge per time on all positive-payoff paths for deployment. Use compact features: log states, squared log states, payoff, payoff squared, cross-sectional min/mean/max, and the gap between the two smallest log states. Store a fallback constant continuation estimate for times with too few positive-payoff samples. Prediction returns the fitted continuation estimate; for zero-payoff states return at least zero.
plan.mechanism: Cross-fitted, exercise-gated ridge with out-of-fold stopping targets. The parent fits continuation values and updates cash flows on the same 256 paths, allowing regression errors to alter their own labels. Cross-fitting breaks this feedback, while restricting regression to positive-payoff states concentrates scarce samples near relevant exercise decisions.
